20261103MA85144.description: Massachusetts Question 1. Makes the legislature and governor subject to public-records laws.
20261103MA85144.summary: This ballot measure would make the legislature and governor subject to public-records laws, with exemptions from disclosing records related to policy development or constituent services.
20261103MA85144.seatName: 1 - Expand Public Records Law to governor and legislative offices

20261103MA85145.description: Massachusetts Question 2. Allows public counsel employees to engage in collective bargaining.
20261103MA85145.summary: This ballot measure would allow collective bargaining for employees of the state Committee for Public Counsel Services, which provides legal representation to people who cannot afford an attorney.
20261103MA85145.seatName: 2 - Allow Committee for Public Counsel Services employees to engage in collective bargaining

20261103MA85146.description: Massachusetts Question 3. Replaces party primaries with an open primary for the top two candidates.
20261103MA85146.summary: This ballot measure would eliminate separate party primaries and adopt an open primary in which the top two vote recipients advance to the general election. It also would require candidates for governor to be paired with a candidate for lieutenant governor in the primary.

20261103MA85147.description: Massachusetts Question 4. Allows voter registration on Election Day.
20261103MA85147.summary: This ballot measure would allow people to register to vote at polling places on Election Day and repeal a requirement to register at least 10 days before an election.

20261103MA85148.description: Massachusetts Question 5. Revises annual limits on state tax revenues.
20261103MA85148.summary: This ballot measure would revise an existing limit on annual tax revenue collections by linking it to growth over the previous year and would include revenue from a millionaires' income tax surcharge in the calculation.
20261103MA85148.seatName: 5 - Modify state tax revenue limit methodology

20261103MA85149.description: Massachusetts Question 6. Creates a state fund for natural resource conservation efforts.
20261103MA85149.summary: This ballot measure would direct sales tax revenue from sporting goods, recreational vehicles and golf courses to a new state fund for natural resource conservation, including water, forest and farm projects, parks and outdoor recreation areas.
20261103MA85149.seatName: 6 - Establish Nature for All conservation fund

20261103MA85150.description: Massachusetts Question 7. Bars local ordinances against single-family homes on certain-sized lots.
20261103MA85150.summary: This ballot measure would bar local ordinances against single-family homes built on residentially zoned lots that have at least 5,000 square feet, 50 feet of frontage and access to public water and sewer service.
20261103MA85150.seatName: 7 - Reduce minimum lot sizes for single-family homes

20261103MA85151.description: Massachusetts Question 8. Repeals the legalization of marijuana for recreational purposes.
20261103MA85151.summary: This ballot measure would repeal laws allowing the legal sale of marijuana for recreational purposes but impose no criminal penalties for possession of less than two ounces. Medical marijuana would remain legal.

20261103MA85152.description: Massachusetts Question 9. Asks voters whether to keep or repeal gun control measures passed in 2024.
20261103MA85152.summary: This referendum asks voters whether to uphold or repeal a 2024 law that expands restrictions on "assault-style" firearms, prohibits "ghost guns" lacking serial numbers, creates an electronic firearm registration system and expands a "red flag" law allowing the temporary removal of guns from people deemed a danger to themselves or others.
